evals.prompt: I want to set up a Zettelkasten like Sönke Ahrens describes, for my reading about acoustics and show design. Put it in ~/zk-test.
evals.expected_output: Runs init_slipbox.py for ~/zk-test, reports the created folders (inbox, literature, permanent, projects, index.md, _templates, _tools), explains the workflow in a few lines, and offers to capture a first fleeting note. Does not create topic folders.

assertions.name: runs-init-script
assertions.description: Uses scripts/init_slipbox.py (or equivalent) so the folders, templates and _tools exist

assertions.name: no-topic-folders
assertions.description: Does not create folders per topic such as acoustics/ under permanent/

assertions.name: short-workflow
assertions.description: Summarises capture -> literature -> permanent -> index in a few lines instead of pasting the whole README

evals.prompt: Here is my fleeting note: 'reverb time depends on room volume and absorption - Sabine'. Turn it into a permanent note for me.
evals.expected_output: Does not just write a note: first asks the user to restate the single idea and how it relates to existing notes (support/contradict/extend/example), searches permanent/ for related notes, then creates the note with --link ID:why (or exempts it only if the box is empty), and marks the fleeting note processed.

assertions.name: asks-connecting-questions
assertions.description: Asks how the idea relates to existing notes before filing it

assertions.name: links-required
assertions.description: Uses at least one --link when other permanent notes exist

assertions.name: marks-processed
assertions.description: Moves the handled fleeting note to inbox/.processed via the processed command

evals.prompt: Check how healthy my slip-box in ~/zettelkasten is.
evals.expected_output: Runs lint.py with --root ~/zettelkasten, reports errors first and warnings second in plain words, includes the stats line, and recommends one or two highest-value fixes instead of dumping every finding.

assertions.name: prioritised
assertions.description: Puts errors before warnings and suggests only a few fixes

evals.prompt: Can you use my slip-box to track my to-do list and release tasks for the app?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a slip-box is for ideas, not tasks, and points to the project-cards skill for task tracking instead of putting tasks into permanent notes.

assertions.name: redirects-tasks
assertions.description: Does not store tasks as permanent notes; points to the project-cards skill
